dialogue.content: 相談者役をさせていただきます。よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: I'll be playing the role of the client. It's nice to meet you.

dialogue.content: 本日はよろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: It's a pleasure to be working with you today.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.content: 時間になりましたので始めさせて頂きますね。
dialogue.English: It's time, so let's get started.

dialogue.content: こんばんは相談員です本日はよろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in today.

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Thank you for seeing me.

dialogue.content: まず始めに性別と年齢を教えて頂けますか？
dialogue.English: First, could you please tell me your gender and age?

dialogue.content: 女性　48歳
dialogue.English: Female, 48 years old.

dialogue.content: 教えて頂きありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that with me.

dialogue.content: 本日はどのようなご相談で来られましたか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 母の介護の事で
dialogue.English: It's about caring for my mother.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。具体的にどのような事でお悩みですか？
dialogue.English: I see. What specifically are you struggling with?

dialogue.content: 介護がつらくて
dialogue.English: The caregiving is just so hard.

dialogue.content: 先が見えない
dialogue.English: I can't see an end in sight.

dialogue.content: そのように思われているのですね、、
dialogue.English: I understand that's how you're feeling...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ええ、ええ。
dialogue.English: Yes, I see.

dialogue.content: いつ頃から悩まれるようになりましたか？
dialogue.English: When did you start feeling this way?

dialogue.content: 最近です
dialogue.English: Recently.

dialogue.content: 母の病気が進んできたせいか
dialogue.English: I think it's because my mother's illness has progressed.

dialogue.content: 気が抜けない
dialogue.English: I can't let my guard down.

dialogue.content: なるほど。目を離せないような感じなのでしょうか
dialogue.English: I see. Does it feel like you can't take your eyes off her?

dialogue.content: はい。パーキンソン病なので
dialogue.English: Yes, because she has Parkinson's disease.

dialogue.content: 症状が進んできて
dialogue.English: The symptoms have been getting worse.

dialogue.content: 体も効かないし、怪我したら大変
dialogue.English: Her body doesn't move well, and it would be terrible if she got injured.

dialogue.content: それだと当然、以前よりもお疲れになりますよね
dialogue.English: That would naturally make you more tired than before, wouldn't it?

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: そうですよね、、
dialogue.English: I can imagine...

dialogue.content: 相談者さんお一人でお母様を介護されているのですか?
dialogue.English: Are you the only one caring for your mother?

dialogue.content: はい。母と2人暮らしなので
dialogue.English: Yes. It's just my mother and I living together.

dialogue.content: デイサービスには行っていますが、基本自分がしています
dialogue.English: She goes to a day service, but I'm basically the one doing everything.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね、、毎日、本当にお疲れさまです
dialogue.English: I see... You must be so exhausted every day.

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: ええ、ええ
dialogue.English: Yes, I understand.

dialogue.content: デイサービスに行かれている間はお仕事をされているのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Are you working while she's at the day service?

dialogue.content: いえ、今は無職です
dialogue.English: No, I'm unemployed right now.

dialogue.content: 何があるかわからないし
dialogue.English: You never know what might happen,

dialogue.content: 仕事は辞めました
dialogue.English: so I quit my job.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。お母様の事を思って退職されたのですね
dialogue.English: I see. You left your job out of concern for your mother.

dialogue.content: はい、心配が尽きなくて、
dialogue.English: Yes, I couldn't stop worrying,

dialogue.content: 家に1人で置いておけなくて
dialogue.English: and I couldn't leave her alone at home.

dialogue.content: 怪我したり急変の心配がありますものね
dialogue.English: Yes, there's always the fear of injury or a sudden change in her condition.

dialogue.content: はい、！
dialogue.English: Yes!

dialogue.content: はい、、でした。
dialogue.English: Yes... that’s how it was.

dialogue.content: ただ、そうなると必然的にずっと家にいることになって息抜きに出かけたりもできませんよね
dialogue.English: But that must mean you're always at home, and you can't go out to take a break, can you?

dialogue.content: パーキンソン病って治らないので
dialogue.English: Parkinson's disease doesn't get better,

dialogue.content: 現状維持か悪くなるだけで
dialogue.English: it either stays the same or gets worse.

dialogue.content: デイサービスに行っている間に片付けや洗濯や掃除、食事を作って
dialogue.English: While she's at the day service, I do the tidying, laundry, cleaning, and cooking,

dialogue.content: そうしないと母の対応は無理で。
dialogue.English: otherwise I can't keep up with her care.

dialogue.content: ええ、ええ。お母様がデイサービスに行かれている間も一息つける訳ではないのですね、、
dialogue.English: I see. So even while your mother is at the day service, it's not like you can take a breather...

dialogue.content: 母がいると母にかかりっきりです
dialogue.English: When my mother is here, I'm completely focused on her.

dialogue.content: 本当にお母様の為に尽くされているのですね
dialogue.English: You are truly devoted to your mother.

dialogue.content: まあ、親なので。娘だし。子どもは私1人なので。
dialogue.English: Well, she's my parent. I'm her daughter. I'm her only child.

dialogue.content: しかも、パーキンソン病は治らないから今よりも元気になってもらえるように介護を頑張ろうとも思えませんものね
dialogue.English: And since Parkinson's isn't curable, it must be hard to motivate yourself with the thought that your care will make her healthier than she is now.

dialogue.content: でも少しでも進行は遅くしたい
dialogue.English: But I want to slow the progression, even just a little.

dialogue.content: ここ一年で急に悪化して
dialogue.English: It's gotten suddenly worse in the past year,

dialogue.content: 歩行器で支えても後ろに倒れるし、
dialogue.English: even with a walker for support, she falls backwards,

dialogue.content: 片付けして怪我しないようにしないといけない
dialogue.English: so I have to keep things tidy so she doesn't get hurt.

dialogue.content: ええ、ええ。一生懸命に尽くされいるのに、報われない気持ちになったりはしませんか？
dialogue.English: I see. Do you ever feel unrewarded, despite all your devoted efforts?

dialogue.content: 報われない、、
dialogue.English: Unrewarded...

dialogue.content: でも母には自分しかいないから
dialogue.English: But my mother only has me.

dialogue.content: 確かにそうだとは思いますが、施設に預けたりもされずお母様の為に日々、尽くされていて相談者さんは本当に母親思いな方だと思いました。
dialogue.English: While I'm sure that's true, the fact that you care for your mother every day without putting her in a facility shows me that you are a truly devoted daughter.

dialogue.content: ここひと月、認知症みたいな状態で
dialogue.English: For the past month, she's been in a state like dementia,

dialogue.content: 夜中に突然叫ぶし
dialogue.English: she suddenly screams in the middle of the night,

dialogue.content: 家に帰ると言って泣いたり
dialogue.English: and cries saying she wants to go home,

dialogue.content: デイサービスでも暴言吐いて
dialogue.English: and she's verbally abusive at the day service,

dialogue.content: 職員の人からと言われました
dialogue.English: the staff there told me.

dialogue.content: そうですか、、相談者さん自身の心も不安定になってしまいませんか？
dialogue.English: I see... Does that make you feel emotionally unstable as well?

dialogue.content: わからない
dialogue.English: I don't know.

dialogue.content: お金がないから、施設に入れるのはできないです
dialogue.English: I don't have the money, so putting her in a facility isn't an option.

dialogue.content: 団地住まいで
dialogue.English: We live in public housing.

dialogue.content: そうなのですねお母様が夜中に叫ばれたりされているみたいなので、なかなかしっかり睡眠は取れないのではないですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Since your mother screams at night, you probably aren't able to get much proper sleep, are you?

dialogue.content: そうですね。あまり寝てはいないです。
dialogue.English: That's right. I don't sleep much.

dialogue.content: でも父も学生の時に亡くして
dialogue.English: But my father also passed away when I was a student,

dialogue.content: 頼れる人はいない
dialogue.English: I have no one to rely on.

dialogue.content: ええ、ええ。自分しかいないと思いながら、1人で全てしないといけないのはしんどいですよね
dialogue.English: Yes, I understand. It must be so difficult to have to do everything by yourself, feeling like you're the only one she has.

dialogue.content: 絶対に
dialogue.English: Absolutely.

dialogue.content: 誰も頼れない
dialogue.English: I can't rely on anyone.

dialogue.content: 母と2人で生きてきたので
dialogue.English: It's always been just me and my mother.

dialogue.content: しかも、この状況がいつまで続くのかも分からないですし
dialogue.English: On top of that, you don't know how long this situation will last.

dialogue.content: 家でお母様を見ておられる時は他に何かされているのですか？
dialogue.English: When you're at home looking after your mother, are you able to do anything else?

dialogue.content: 例えば本を読まれたり
dialogue.English: Like reading a book, for example?

dialogue.content: 母の世話ばかりです
dialogue.English: I do nothing but take care of her.

dialogue.content: あとは自分のお風呂とか最低限のこと
dialogue.English: Other than that, just the bare minimum, like taking a bath myself.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 気分転換になるようなものはなかなかないような感じなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Does it feel like there's nothing you can do to change your mood or take a break?

dialogue.content: 最近母が下痢ぎみで
dialogue.English: Recently, my mother has been having diarrhea,

dialogue.content: 漏らしたりもして
dialogue.English: and sometimes she has accidents,

dialogue.content: 排泄物を片付けていると涙が出ます
dialogue.English: When I'm cleaning up her waste, I just start crying.

dialogue.content: それは目が離せないし、気分転換する余裕がなさそうですね、、
dialogue.English: It sounds like you can't take your eyes off her, and there's no room to take a break...

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 相談者さんのお体は大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.English: Are you doing okay physically?

dialogue.content: はい、、
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: それだけの生活をされていて
dialogue.English: Living a life like that...

dialogue.content: すみません途中ですが、時間になりましたので終わらせて頂いてもよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I'm sorry to interrupt, but our time is up. Is it alright if we conclude for today?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 貴重な時間を頂きありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your valuable time.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: おかげさまで大変勉強になりました。またよろしくお願い致します
dialogue.English: This has been a great learning experience for me. I look forward to our next session.

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much.)

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございましたそれでは失礼致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well. I'll take my leave now.
